policy.activities: Optional activities array contains standalone worksheet/reading resources, distinct from the real-demo catalog. Sections reference activities by id; render both section.demos and section.activities, filtering course membership and deduplicating within a unit.
policy.acoustics: Acoustics (2026-10-23, Steve) is a module, not a syllabus course: Vol 1 ch 16 and 17 plus a Beyond the textbook unit that lists demos directly (unit.demos). Its units use requirement module. A section shared with another course keeps its unit there and names its acoustics unit in unit_in.
policy.modules: Thermodynamics and Modern Physics (2026-10-24, Steve) are modules like Acoustics: Thermodynamics is Vol 2 ch 1 to 4, Modern Physics is Vol 3 ch 5 to 11 (relativity through cosmology). Their units use requirement module and follow the textbook chapters. Physics II ends with AC circuits (Vol 2 ch 15, before ch 16), light and geometric optics (Vol 3 ch 1 and 2) and wave optics (Vol 3 ch 3 and 4); none is optional (Steve, 2026-10-24). Demos from Misc that serve these sections moved into them; demos from other courses that serve a section here also list the module.
policy.astro: Astronomy (2026-10-24, Steve) is a module like the others: every astronomy demo, in four units (sky, gravitation and orbits from Vol 1 ch 13, stars, galaxies and cosmology from Vol 3 10.6, 11.6, 11.7). Demos stay in their other courses too. Demos with no section here are listed in unit.demos, which may also hold a demo whose sections belong to another course (e-over-m in Modern). Ising moved to Thermodynamics (Beyond the textbook) and e-over-m to Modern Physics; Misc keeps only bz-reaction and dna, under one heading.

units.title: First lab: waves on a string
Topic 1 · Intro material
units.note: The size of the solar system: distances in astronomical units, light travel times and powers of ten.

units.title: Topic 2 · Star charts and motion of the Sun and Moon
units.note: Positions on the sky, the Sun along the ecliptic and the seasons, the phases of the Moon, eclipses and precession.

units.title: Topic 3 · Planetary motion, the Copernican revolution and gravity
units.note: From Earth centered models to Kepler’s laws and Newton’s gravity, and weighing the Sun and planets with orbits.

units.title: Topic 4 · Telescopes, light and the electromagnetic spectrum
units.note: How telescopes gather and resolve light, the spectrum from radio to X rays, thermal radiation and spectral lines.

units.title: Topic 5 · Formation of planetary systems
units.note: A spinning cloud flattens into a disk and builds planets; what sets a planet’s temperature, and the habitable zone.

units.title: Topic 6 · The Earth and Moon system
units.note: The Moon forming impact, craters and the ages of surfaces, why small worlds cool first, and the geology of the Earth.

units.title: Topic 7 · Inner planets to Mars I
units.note: Mercury, Venus and Mars compared with Earth: spin, atmospheres, greenhouse warming and surfaces.

units.title: Topic 8 · Mars II, geology
units.note: Volcanoes, canyons, old water and crater counts on Mars, and its two small moons.

units.title: Topic 9 · Minor planets and the asteroid belt
units.note: The asteroid belt, the largest asteroids, near Earth asteroids, and how Jupiter shapes small bodies’ orbits.

units.title: Topic 10 · Outer planets: Jupiter and Saturn
units.note: The gas giants, their rings and their moons, and the tidal forces that heat moons and limit rings.

units.title: Topic 11 · Uranus, Neptune and the Kuiper belt
units.note: The ice giants, Uranus’s tipped axis, Pluto and the Kuiper belt, and comets.

units.title: Topic 12 · Exoplanets
units.note: Finding planets around other stars by their pull and their shadows, and what they are made of.

units.title: 1 · Sources and decay
units.note: Decay laws, the medical isotopes and the ⁹⁹Mo to ⁹⁹ᵐTc generator with transient equilibrium, Q values for isotope production, and the X-ray tube with its filtration and half value layer.

units.title: 2 · Photon interactions
units.note: Compton kinematics and the Klein–Nishina cross section, attenuation coefficients from XCOM, and the photoelectric effect as review.

units.title: 3 · Charged particles in matter
units.note: Single Coulomb scattering, the step that multiple scattering adds up, then stopping power and range.

units.title: 4 · Dosimetry and detectors
units.note: Dose rate from a point source, absorbed dose against equivalent dose, and a scintillation detector with its calibration and resolution.

units.title: 5 · Radiobiology
units.note: Cell survival, fractionation and the relative biological effectiveness of protons.

units.title: 6 · Protection and shielding
units.note: Time, distance and shielding: dose rate from a point source, broad beam transmission and buildup in lead, concrete and water, and a barrier calculation for a PET uptake room with workload, occupancy and the NCRP design goals (Dose view of Nuclear Reactions).

units.title: 7 · Proton therapy
units.note: Preparation for the seniors’ QA runs and dosimetry walkthrough at the proton therapy center, modeled on its IBA Proteus ONE pencil beam scanning system: the spread out Bragg peak, the morning QA and patient plan checks, a TRS-398 beam calibration and the RBE of protons.

units.title: 8 · Photon and electron beams
units.note: Second phase.

coming.title: Linac Beams in Water
coming.note: Percent depth dose for megavoltage photons and electrons from published reference data, buildup, field size and SSD, and several photon beams against one proton field.

units.title: 9 · Imaging
units.note: Echo ranging, impedance, tissue attenuation in dB per cm per MHz and Doppler; the Larmor relation for hydrogen. X-ray imaging, MRI and nuclear medicine imaging come in a second phase.
